Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Trainer creates a new Exam and manually authors Exam-specific questions.
column3: 1. Log in as a VERIFIED Trainer. 2. Open Trainer > Exams > "Create New Exam". 3. Enter the Exam title. 4. Manually author single-choice questions one by one.
column4: The Exam is created in DRAFT/PRIVATE state; each authored question is scoped privately to this Exam and is not shared with or pulled from the reusable Question Bank used by Course Quizzes. There is no minimum-question requirement enforced while authoring (see SYS_FLOW_EXM_TC04).
column5: - Trainer role, VERIFIED profile.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Trainer/Course Manager builds an Exam using the criteria-based Exam Matrix auto-generator, which pulls only from the caller's OWN authored question bank.
column3: 1. Open "Create New Exam" > "Import by Matrix". 2. Define criteria (Skill/Difficulty distribution). 3. Tap Generate.
column4: The matrix draws questions ONLY from the caller's own authored questions — never platform-wide — and assembles the Exam. If the caller has not personally authored enough matching questions for a criterion, generation fails clearly with a "Not enough questions in bank for criteria...: Required N, Found M" message instead of a partial/empty exam.
column5: - Trainer or Course Manager role holding enough of their own authored questions matching the matrix criteria.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Trainer bulk-imports one or more Exams and their questions via the Exam Excel template.
column3: 1. Download Hango_Exam_Import_Template.xlsx via "Import by Excel". 2. Fill in the EXAM and QUESTIONS sheets with valid rows. 3. Upload the file.
column4: The import succeeds; each imported Exam is created as DRAFT, version "v0.1", with all its questions attached and scoped privately; a success summary shows totalExamsCreated / totalQuestionsImported.
column5: - Trainer role; a filled copy of the template ready.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: The documented "fixed 40-question / 50-minute" Exam format is NOT enforced anywhere in the current app — an incomplete or oversized Exam can be saved, submitted for review, and even published with no question-count or duration check.
column3: 1. Author or import an Exam with far fewer than 40 questions (e.g. 3) and an unusual duration (e.g. 5 minutes). 2. Save it. 3. Submit it for review (or Publish directly as a Course Manager).
column4: Every step succeeds with no validation error at any stage — creation, question-saving, submit-for-review, and publish all accept the non-conforming Exam as-is. Only the 0-10 scoring SCALE is actually hardcoded (score = 10 × correctCount / questionCount in ExamService.saveExamAttempt); question COUNT and DURATION are freely whatever the author set, confirmed by direct backend review (no expectedQuestionCount check exists in ExamService or CourseManagerExamMatrixServiceImpl). Document the actual observed behavior even though it contradicts the intended business rule.
column5: - Trainer/Course Manager role able to author or import an Exam.

column4: The Exam persists in DRAFT state, editable, and does not yet appear in the Learner-facing public Exam list.
column5: - An in-progress Exam exists.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Trainer submits a complete Exam for Course Manager review.

column4: The Exam moves into the Course Manager's Exams-for-review queue; it remains hidden from the public Exam list until published.
column5: - A Draft Exam owned by a Trainer.

column4: The Exam becomes published/visible in the Learner-facing Exam list; the Trainer receives a ContentApproved notification.
column5: - A submitted Exam exists in the review queue.

column4: The Exam returns to a Rejected/Draft-editable state, visible only to the Trainer with the reason attached; the Trainer receives a ContentRejected notification.
column5: - A different submitted Exam exists.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Learner starts a published Exam and sees its full question set with a countdown timer that runs entirely on the device — the timer is NOT synced from any server-recorded start/end time.
column3: 1. Open a published Exam. 2. Tap Start. 3. Observe the question count and the countdown.
column4: The Exam's actual saved question count (author-set, not necessarily 40 per SYS_FLOW_EXM_TC04) is presented, single-choice; a countdown starts from the Exam's configured duration using ONLY the device clock. Confirmed by direct backend review: ExamController has no "start attempt" endpoint and the submit request body carries only {score, answers} — the server never records or checks a start/end time for the attempt.
column5: - A published Exam exists.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Answers are cached locally during the exam so closing/reopening the app does not lose progress.
column3: 1. Start an Exam attempt and answer 10-15 questions. 2. Close and reopen the app (or navigate away and back) before submitting. 3. Resume the same attempt.
column4: Previously answered questions are restored from the take_exam_<examId> SharedPreferences cache instead of resetting to blank; the countdown continues from wherever the device clock puts it (see SYS_FLOW_EXM_TC11 — not from any server value).
column5: - An in-progress Exam attempt exists on the same device.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Learner submits the Exam and the server recomputes the score independently from the stored correct answers, ignoring any client-calculated value.
column3: 1. Answer all questions, deliberately getting a known number correct/incorrect. 2. Submit.
column4: The returned/stored score equals 10 × (correct count) / totalQuestions, HALF_UP to 2dp, computed server-side in ExamService.saveExamAttempt directly from question_options.is_correct — not from whatever score the Flutter client might locally tally (contrast with the Lesson Quiz's SYS_FLOW_LRN_TC09, which has no such server check).
column5: - A published Exam with a known-correct answer set exists.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: The app auto-submits when its local timer reaches 0, but the server itself never checks how much time has actually elapsed — a submission arriving any amount of time after the intended deadline is still accepted and scored normally.
column3: 1. Start an Exam and let the local timer run down without manually submitting; observe the auto-submit at 0:00. 2. Separately, on a new attempt, answer questions then deliberately wait well past the exam's configured duration before actually sending the submit request.
column4: Step 1: the app calls submit automatically right at 0:00 (client-side auto-submit in take_exam_page.dart). Step 2: the late submission is ALSO accepted and scored 200 OK with no rejection or flag. Confirmed by direct backend review: ExamService.saveExamAttempt has no elapsed-time or deadline check at all; startedAt is even back-computed as (now − durationMinutes) purely for display, never validated against anything — there is no grace-window/late-rejection behavior in the current code.
column5: - Ability to start an Exam attempt and delay a submit request for testing.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Rapid double-submission of the same in-progress attempt is not deduplicated — each Submit call creates its own independent scored ExamAttempt row.
column3: 1. Fill in answers for an Exam attempt. 2. Trigger Submit twice in quick succession (e.g. double-tap the Submit button, or a slow connection causing a retried request).
column4: Both calls succeed 200 OK; TWO separate ExamAttempt rows are persisted for what the Learner experienced as one sitting. Confirmed by direct backend review: ExamService.saveExamAttempt always computes the next attempt number and inserts a new row, with no idempotency key or lock preventing a second concurrent submit. The Learner's Attempt History shows two entries instead of one.
column5: - An Exam attempt ready to submit; a way to trigger two rapid submit calls.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Learner retakes the same Exam an unlimited number of times on separate occasions, each attempt recorded independently — by design, not a bug.
column3: 1. Take the same published Exam 3 separate times, on different sessions, with different answer patterns.
column4: All 3 attempts are recorded independently with their own scores; nothing blocks a retake; Attempt History lists all 3 with correct attempt numbers 1-3.
column5: - A published Exam already attempted once.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Immediately after submitting, the Result/Review Answers screen shows both the correct total score AND an accurate per-question correct/incorrect breakdown with the right answer highlighted.
column3: 1. Immediately after submitting (SYS_FLOW_EXM_TC13), open the Result screen, then the "Review Answers" view.
column4: The total score (0-10 scale) displays correctly, AND each question shows the Learner's selected option plus the actual correct option, marked Correct/Incorrect. This is a regression check: ExamAttemptResponseDTO's answers/correctness/correctAnswers maps are populated correctly from the stored answersJson (ExamService.mapToAttemptDTO), so the previously-documented answers-echo gap is NOT reproducible in the current code by direct review. If the per-question breakdown instead renders empty, that is a NEW regression to report, not the expected legacy behavior.
column5: - A just-submitted Exam attempt exists.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Reopening Attempt History for an older attempt shows the same correct per-question breakdown as the immediate result.
column3: 1. Open the Exam's Attempt History from My Learning. 2. Select an older completed attempt (not the most recent one). 3. Open its "Review Answers" view.
column4: The total score and the per-question correct/incorrect + correct-answer highlighting both render correctly for the historical attempt too, consistent with SYS_FLOW_EXM_TC17 — confirming the fix is stable across fresh and stored attempts, not just the immediate post-submit response.
column5: - At least 2 completed Exam attempts exist in history.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: While an Exam attempt is in progress, the question payload never exposes which option is correct.
column3: 1. Start an Exam attempt. 2. 🔍 Inspect the question-list data the app received for this attempt (browser/dev network tools on the web build, or an intercepting proxy).
column4: The in-progress question payload contains no isCorrect / is_correct field or equivalent flag for any option — correctness is only ever revealed after submission via the scored result.
column5: - An in-progress Exam attempt.

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: An anonymous status-filter query leaks non-public Exam metadata — the Exam list only defaults to PUBLISHED when no status is requested at all.
column3: 1. Log out (or use a no-auth session). 2. 🔍 Use the browser Network tab or a direct request to call the Exam list endpoint with a non-default status filter (e.g. status=DRAFT) — a value never sent by the normal Exam-list screen, which never passes a status param.
column4: The response actually contains DRAFT (and other non-public status) Exams — title, description, creatorName, rejectionReason — visible to a fully anonymous caller. The backend applies the PUBLISHED-only default ONLY when status is entirely omitted, not once any value is supplied (confirmed current gap). The Learner-facing Exam list screen itself never triggers this since it never sends a status param, but the underlying endpoint has no auth/role gate preventing it from being called directly.
column5: - At least one DRAFT/SUBMITTED/REJECTED exam exists; ability to issue one direct API call (e.g. via browser DevTools console) for this verification step.

column4: Every stage transitions correctly end-to-end; the final scored attempt is available for downstream Weakness Analysis / Recommendation (see SYS_FLOW_PWY and SYS_FLOW_AIR flows).

Exam Authoring- Matrix Generation- Revie: Trainer/Course Manager opens the read-only Exam History dialog and sees a chronological timeline of everything that happened to the Exam (create, edit, submit, reject, publish, hide/unhide) - a plain append-only log, unlike Course versioning which spawns a new version row per change.
